 IMD update: Weather alert raised to depression, heavy rain likely for TN, Puducherry
 Evolving Bay system presents two distinct weather scenarios: an expansive spell of rain, thunderstorms over South Peninsula and prospects of a powerful storm tracking elsewhere
 By Vinson Kurian 
 Updated - November 11, 2026 at 04:20 PM. × Share
 WhatsApp X Facebook LinkedIn Messenger Reddit Mail https://www.thehindubusinessline.com/economy/agri-business/imd-update-isolated-heavy-rain-likely-for-tn-puducherry-as-fresh-low-brews/article71688439.ece Copy 
 The depression likely to form over south-west Bay of Bengal on Sunday may lie close to Sri Lanka and south Tamil Nadu coast by midnight, according to the ECMWF-AIFS model.
 | Photo Credit:
 www.meteologix.com/in
 India Meteorological Department (IMD) has upgraded its outlook for a fresh low-pressure area forming over the south-east Bay of Bengal on Friday, to that of a depression by Sunday. The system is the latest in a succession of monsoon disturbances, two of whose predecessors went on to develop into powerful cyclones , Arnab and Murasu , that struck the Andhra Pradesh coast so far during an eventful north-east monsoon season.
 The IMD identified a parent cyclonic circulation over the South Andaman Sea on Wednesday, which is expected to descend to the lower levels of the atmosphere and consolidate into the new ‘low’ by Friday. It may initially north-westwards, become well-marked by Saturday and intensify further into a depression on Sunday. This rapid, linear progression has become a notable feature of monsoon systems in a warming climate.
 Enough time and space
 Significantly, the system is expected to remain close to its area of formation through the first three days, giving it time and room to consolidate before embarking on a possible journey towards land. Potential destinations include India’s east coast to the west-northwest; Myanmar or Bangladesh to the east-northeast; or even Sri Lanka to the west-southwest. However, forecast models have yet to converge on either its intensification potential or its eventual trajectory and landfall destination.
 Ocean conditions currently offer an important source of support for the developing system. Sea-surface temperatures across its prospective area of formation are exceptionally warm at 29-30°C, providing abundant supply of moisture, essential fuel for intensification. Temperatures are only marginally lower, at around 28°C, along the Andhra Pradesh and Odisha coasts, presumably reflecting the cooling effect of the heavy rainfall associated with the predecessor cyclones making landfalls during end-October.
 Wind shear value not ideal
 Wind shear conditions were not particularly favourable as of Wednesday, but model projections indicate that they could ease progressively, creating a more conducive environment for the system to strengthen. The combination of exceptionally warm seas and potentially improving atmospheric conditions will therefore bear close watching as the Bay prepares for yet another round of cyclonic activity.
 Heavy rain for TN, Puducherry
 As things stand this Wednesday, the developing Bay system presents two distinct weather scenarios: an increasingly expansive spell of rain and thunderstorms over the South Peninsula in the immediate term, and the prospect of a potentially powerful storm whose intensity and eventual destination remain far from settled.
 The IMD has for now forecast isolated heavy rainfall over Tamil Nadu , Puducherry and Karaikal on Wednesday, with another spell likely on Sunday and Monday. Kerala and Mahe could also see isolated heavy rain on Monday. The rain footprint is expected to expand over the weekend. Fairly widespread to widespread rainfall is likely over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal on Sunday, extending to Kerala and Mahe on Monday.
 Thunderstorms, lightning
 Isolated to scattered rainfall is forecast over Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal over the four days beginning Wednesday and again on Monday; over Kerala and Mahe for five days from Wednesday; and over Lakshadweep for six days. Coastal and South Interior Karnataka are likely to receive rain on Sunday and Monday, while coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema could see showers over three days beginning Saturday.
 Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal are likely to experience thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds of 40-50 km/hr, gusting to 60 km/hr, on Wednesday and Thursday and again on Sunday and Monday. Isolated thunderstorms and lightning are also forecast over these areas on Friday and Saturday; over Kerala and Mahe and Lakshadweep on Wednesday and Thursday; and over Rayalaseema on Saturday.
 Evolution, trajectory
 The real intrigue, however, lies in evolution and trajectory of the Bay system. The IMD has placed it under watch for intensification into a well-marked ‘low’ by Saturday as it initially moves north-westwards. Global tracking models suggest further intensification into a storm, but are sharply divided over its eventual destination.
 Some simulations point towards India’s east coast, particularly Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh; others favour a track towards Sri Lanka. Yet another set of projections takes the system east-northeast towards Bangladesh and Myanmar. The IMD’s numerical weather prediction models indicate a system that could develop into a deep depression, if not a cyclone, before turning east-north-eastwards across the Bay towards central Myanmar.
